title: Dedicated reservation lattice and graceful fallback safety plan for capacity-to-hosted routing
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Customers on Dedicated pools occasionally observe dropped or significantly delayed requests when local capacity is transiently exhausted. Existing hosted fallback behavior is functional but opaque to tenants and can violate SLAs without clear throttling or tenant guarantees. Goal: design a deterministic "reservation lattice" and graceful fallback policy that minimizes unexpected SLA violations, provides predictable tenant visibility, and prevents cascades when hosted capacity is used as a backstop.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Requests are routed to hosted only after deterministic soft-reserve checks and a documented grace window per tenant.
2) When hosted fallback is used, latency-tail SLA impact per tenant must be estimated and surfaced in the Console.
3) Circuit-breaker prevents more than X% of a tenant's traffic from being remoted to hosted for more than Y minutes without human approval.
4) Rollout plan includes dark launch (shadow routing) and progressive increment with automated rollback if error budget burn is detected.
design_decisions: Use per-tenant soft-reserve tokens: tenants accrue ephemeral credit during low utilization to allow short bursts without triggering hosted fallback.
Introduce a three-state routing decision: LocalPrefer (serve locally unless hard capacity exhausted), SoftReserveDrain (use soft-reserve tokens before hosted), and HostedBackstop.
Limit hosted fallback rate with tenant-specific max-fallback-percent and global safety cap to avoid overloading hosted pools.
Expose explainability metadata in the routing response header (route.reason, route.reservation_used, route.fallback_percent) for debugging and Console visualization.
tradeoffs_and_notes: Pros: Predictable tenant behavior, fewer surprise SLA violations, and better isolation of hosted load spikes.
Cons: Slightly more complex state management in the orchestrator and additional telemetry cost for token accounting.
Edge case: Network partitions between region allocator and capacity adjudicator will default to conservative mode (favor hosted) — needs explicit runbook.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Add soft-reserve ledger and per-tenant config (max_reserve_seconds, max_fallback_percent). Unit tests + integration tests in staging.
Phase 2: Implement graceful fallback circuit-breaker and response headers. Add Console telemetry plumbing for fallback_percent and reservation consumption.
Phase 3: Dark launch routing via shadowing 1% traffic from a cohort of tenants. Monitor fail metrics and customer impact.
Phase 4: Progressive rollout with canary config and auto-rollback tied to error budget and latency SLO thresholds.

qa_notes: Test scenarios: sustained burst that exhausts soft-reserve, rapid oscillation of capacity causing frequent flip between local/hosted, network partition to allocator.
Required metrics: fallback_percent per tenant, reservation_tokens_consumed, hosted_tail_latency_by_tenant, global_hosted_utilization.
Failure modes: token ledger drift (fix: periodic reconciliation and reconcile endpoint), circuit-breaker stuck closed (fix: admin override and healthcheck).
